key_concepts: Earth rotates on its axis approximately once every 24 hours.
Earth's rotation direction is from west to east or counterclockwise.
Earth revolves around the Sun in a counterclockwise direction.
One revolution takes about 365¼ days, or one year.
Rotation causes the apparent movement of the Sun.
Earth receives different amounts of sunlight at different times of the year.
Half of Earth is lighted because that half faces the Sun.
Summer begins in the Northern Hemisphere around June 21 or 22.
The longest daylight period in the Northern Hemisphere occurs around June 21 or 22.
